title: Derived termwise global sections with finite evaluation and transition normalization
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ an inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative rings. Write $\mathscr S(B)$ for strict semilinear systems of module sheaves, with componentwise exactness, identified with modules over $B$ on the sequence site $\mathcal T=\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\ge1}$ [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]. Use unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $A$ be a sheaf of commutative rings with compatible maps $A\to B_n$. Let $U:D(\mathscr S(B))\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(A)))$ be exact termwise scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. The termwise global-sections functor on constant-$A$ towers has a total right derived functor $R\Gamma^{\operatorname{Tow}}_{\mathcal C}$, computed by a K-injective resolution in the constant-$A$ tower category [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Consequently $$G=R\Gamma^{\operatorname{Tow}}_{\mathcal C}\circ U:D(\mathscr S(B))\longrightarrow D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))$$ is an actual functor on the ordinary derived category of strict systems. There are specified natural isomorphisms $$e_nG(J)\cong R\Gamma(\mathcal C,\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B_n}J_n)\cong R\Gamma(\mathcal C,J_n),$$ the last expression computed in $B_n$-modules and then regarded as an abelian complex. The first comparison is induced by evaluating the same constant-$A$ tower resolution; the second is the derived direct-image composition comparison for scalar restriction followed by global sections. These isomorphisms intertwine the actual tower transitions with the maps of derived sections induced by $J_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{B_{n+1}\to B_n}J_n$. They are natural for input derived morphisms. No assertion that varying-ring evaluation preserves K-injectives is made.

proof.text: Construct U^0 explicitly: its nth module is restriction along A to B_n, and its arrows are the given semilinear transitions followed by the scalar-composition identification. The strict-system identity and composition equations verify the functor laws on sections. Evaluation identifies it with the exact coefficient restriction of the nth system evaluation, so it preserves finite limits and colimits componentwise. Localize it and its evaluation comparisons to obtain U.

proof.text: Module sheaves on the essentially small site are Grothendieck in the coefficient universe by lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-coefficient-universe. A separator of the constant-coefficient tower category is the coproduct, over the natural-number indices, of evaluation left adjoints of a separator of modules. Evaluation detects inequality of natural transformations; its adjunction proves that this family separates. Filtered colimits and their exactness are computed pointwise. Thus this tower category is Grothendieck in the same coefficient universe. Obtain K-injective resolutions and derive additive sections by the K-injective localizer: a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence, and additive sections preserve that equivalence.

proof.text: Use the comparison-descent and derived-extensionality argument of lem-coef-tower-right-derived-evaluation for the chosen derived pairs. Exact evaluation factors turn the two units into transformations with the same source. Both are invertible on K-injective towers because constant-coefficient evaluation preserves K-injectivity. Descend their comparison to the derived category. Naturality of the units and the localized transition factors imply its actual-transition identity after cancellation on K-injectives; derived extensionality extends it to all objects. Define G as this tower-derived functor after U.

source.place: Tags 0941 and 0D6E; exact restriction, K-injective computation and normalized derived-unit comparison.

proof.text: Apply lem-coef-restriction-sections-acyclic to a K-injective S-complex and a K-injective resolution of its scalar restriction. Naturality of the R-derived unit and its invertibility at that resolution show that the R-unit is already invertible at the restricted complex. Descend the S-unit and restricted R-unit to an invertible scalar comparison. This gives exactly scalar_unit, including the canonical exact localization factors. Precompose the composite of two scalar comparisons with the derived unit; its normalization, naturality and the exact restriction-composition factors give the same unit equation as the direct comparison. The universal property of right derivation proves the cocycle.

proof.text: Localize the ordinary compatibility of U^0 with system transitions. Its equality on complexes follows from the recorded sectionwise transition equation; the canonical exact localization factors give the equality on the derived category. Combine this equality with the tower comparison transition equation. Naturality of the scalar comparison moves the system transition across it, and the cocycle cancels the two scalar comparisons into the inverse comparison for B_n to B_m. This is finite_transition. All maps used are natural transformations, so naturality in the derived input is retained. Use the already proved exact-square factorization helper of lem-pod-derived-exact-square-composition to normalize the evaluation squares, rather than reproving that factorization.
